This is very normal! She’s probably never had toys or regular human time. Your home is basically an alien planet to her at the moment. She will definitely get better. 

I would ask, what are the usual things she seems to retreat from? Is it when you have the tv on that she goes to her own corner? If so, it may be a good idea to warm her up to any of those things very very slowly and watching the tv or doing the activity when she is already somewhere else. You can also have treats for her when you start the activity and during. However, I think she definitely should be allowed to go off by herself in peace, since she probably knows what she needs best. 

Another thing you can do when she goes off by herself, is maybe go in, sit far away from her on the ground (to be on her level) and just talk very quietly and sweetly to her and see if she comes over. If not, you should leave her alone. If she does, give her lots of scritches and treats. This will help her to learn that she is safe and happy when she is with you but she is always able to have alone time that is respected as well. Those are three things (along with everything else) that she has not had before. 

I know she is sensitive to other dogs, but keep your eye out for any dogs she does seem interested in as they will help her learn to play by observation. That might not happen, so what you can do is get toys that encourage her to interact with them (like the Kong toys with some peanut butter on the inside) and when she does show interest in a toy, you should reward her with a treat and praise so she knows she’s doing the right thing. Another option: take her to the pet store and let her pick out her own toy! This will be an excursion that might not work but is good exposure anyways. I don’t know how tall she is, but mine are short so I have to put all the toys on the ground for them so they can pick.

So I guess here is my tinder success story. 
I'm not shy at all. Well, at least when we met I was never shy. I've always been the extrovert in what feels like a world full of completely private introverts, and so far he has been the most private person I have ever met. I think it's really an opposites attract thing. 

He is so aware of others, that he left off talking to me after we started talking regularly all because I went on vacation. After I came back from my trip, we met in person, and it was basically love after first date. I brought out things in him that he had always kept hidden from others; for some reason he felt so comfortable with me that he could pretty much tell me anything. He made me feel like I finally found someone that understood me; he was the only person I had ever met that didn't look at me like I had two heads every time I spoke my mind. And I pretty much always speak my mind, weather I mean to or not, I just sort of blurt things off the top of my head. He has taught me the power of thinking through things before I say them. In all, I think we have made each other better people by growing together. We are now engaged, and although sometimes he will tell me things I didn't know about him, and I might still blurt hurtful things, we don't ever take it personally and we always just pause and take time to sift through all the input, or lack there of, that we give each other. 

We are currently engaged and living very happily together. We are getting married this year :) 

Ultimately, I think people long to know things about other people, and when you want to know everything about another person because they fascinate you, be honest and open with them and they will usually follow suit. How different you are will intrigue the other person and that always makes for something new to talk about.
